content:
As the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have risen by US$100 compared to the previous generation, Apple has extended the price hike to the entire iPhone lineup, including models whose specifications remain completely unchanged.

This means the starting price of the iPhone 17 has increased from US$799 to US$899. At the same time, the iPhone Air's starting price has officially broken through the US$1,000 mark, set at US$1,099.

The iPhone 17e and iPhone 16 have also seen the same US$100 price increase. The iPhone 17e has been raised from the original US$599 to US$699.

This situation will naturally deter consumers — these iPhone models have been on the market for a year, yet their prices have been raised without any changes.

However, Apple has always adjusted prices in response to market conditions, such as rising costs of components including RAM and storage, and this time the increase is only US$100, lower than what some analysts had originally anticipated.

Below is the complete iPhone pricing after today's adjustment:

  • iPhone 17e: 256GB, US$699
  • iPhone 16: 128GB, US$799
  • iPhone 17: 256GB, US$899
  • iPhone Air: 256GB, US$1,099
  • iPhone 18 Pro: 256GB, US$1,199
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: 256GB, US$1,299
  • iPhone Duo: 256GB, US$1,999

With the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 17 Pro has been discontinued. The entry-level iPhone 17 is expected to be replaced by a new iPhone in spring 2027.

Apple has staggered its product release cycle, with only high-end new models debuting this autumn, while updated versions of the entry-level and Air models are expected to launch between March and April next year.
